summary: From a legacy PDL v1 model (legacy.pdl, the TPKT model of plugins/): import keeps the SDK's id and name, which validate refuses, and a struct name the SDK also has, which the build refuses once the hook that attaches the protocol to TCP port 102 includes the SDK's TCP header; init's sample test fails until it is removed.

runs.note: Drop init's sample model, pin the profile, and add packet tests from RFC 1006 (the corpus's, for this project's name and id).

model.name-taken and model.id-taken: use init's label and id, which src/rfc1006_impl.c is written for. Add the parent (PDL v1 has none): TCP's header has no fixed length, so no classify; attach it to port 102 in rfc1006_hook_register_parents.

edits.new:
profile: "1.10.2"
parents:
  - protocol: tcp    # port 102: attached in rfc1006_hook_register_parents

runs.note: build.cc in generated/rfc1006_mmt_plugin.h: the struct tpkthdr of the old model is also an SDK struct (tcpip/mmt_tcpip_attributes.h, which the hook's PROTO_TCP brings in). The generated code comes from the model: rename the struct there.
rfc1006/basic is init's sample of its own header (version, kind, length), not of RFC 1006: delete it.
